s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes was created by the 65th Constitutional Amendment, 1990.
2. The separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes came into being on 19 February 2004.
3. The National Commission for Backward Classes was given constitutional status by the 101st Constitutional Amendment, 2018.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct: the 65th Amendment (1990, in force 1992) created the combined commission, and the NCST came into being on 19 Feb 2004 after the 89th Amendment. 3 is wrong: the NCBC got constitutional status (Art. 338B) by the 102nd Amendment, 2018, not the 101st.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional status of backward classes:
1. The 103rd Amendment (2021) restored the power of the States to keep their own lists of SEBCs.
2. The 102nd Amendment inserted Article 342A, under which the President notifies the socially and educationally backward classes.
3. The 102nd Amendment relieved the National Commission for Scheduled Castes of work relating to backward classes.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct: the 102nd Amendment (2018) inserted Art. 342A and removed backward-class work from the NCSC. 1 is wrong: it was the 105th Amendment (2021), not the 103rd, that restored the States' power to keep their own SEBC lists.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In 1978 a non-statutory Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes was set up by a resolution.
2. The creation of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs in 1999 paved the way for a separate commission for Scheduled Tribes.
3. The National Commission for Women and the National Commission for Minorities are constitutional bodies like the National Commission for Scheduled Castes.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 2). The 1978 commission was set up by resolution, and the 1999 Ministry of Tribal Affairs led to the 89th Amendment split. 3 is wrong: NCW, NCM, NHRC and NCPCR are statutory bodies; only NCSC, NCST, NCBC and the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities are directly established by the Constitution.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commissions for SCs, STs and Backward Classes:
1. Each consists of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three other members.
2. The members are appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal for a term of five years.
3. The statutory NCBC under the 1993 Act was headed by a retired judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the President does appoint them by warrant under his hand and seal, but the term fixed by the President's Rules (2004) is three years (not more than two terms), not five.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Commission for Scheduled Castes submits its annual reports to the Prime Minister, who lays them before Parliament.
2. Under the 2005 Rules the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes also deals with ownership of minor forest produce by tribals.
3. While investigating a matter, the National Commission for Scheduled Castes has all the powers of a civil court trying a suit, but it cannot punish.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct: the NCST's 2005 Rules add minor forest produce, mineral and water rights, rehabilitation and PESA; under Art. 338(8) the Commission has civil-court powers but its advice is only recommendatory. 1 is wrong: reports go to the President, not the Prime Minister; the President lays them before Parliament with an action-taken memorandum.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities:
1. The office, designated Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities, works under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
2. Its headquarters is at New Delhi, with regional offices at Belgaum, Chennai and Kolkata.
3. The Constitution does not fix the qualifications, tenure, salary or removal of the Special Officer.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities works under the Ministry of Minority Affairs, not Home Affairs. There is a single officer for the whole country, appointed by the President.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Commission)
a. National Commission for Scheduled Castes
b. National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
c. National Commission for Backward Classes
d. National Commission for Minorities
List-II (Chairperson as of 2026)
i. Antar Singh Arya
ii. Harjit Singh Grewal
iii. Kishor Makwana
iv. Niranjan Jyoti
x: NCSC – Kishor Makwana (from Mar 2024); NCST – Antar Singh Arya; NCBC – Niranjan Jyoti (Jun 2026); NCM – Harjit Singh Grewal (Jul 2026): a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Event)
a. First Backward Classes Commission under Kaka Kalelkar
b. Second Backward Classes Commission under B.P. Mandal
c. First reservation policy in Kolhapur under Shahu Maharaj
d. Indra Sawhney v. Union of India judgment
List-II (Year)
i. 1902
ii. 1953
iii. 1979
iv. 1992
x: Kalelkar Commission – 29 Jan 1953 (ii); Mandal Commission – 1 Jan 1979, Janata government (iii); Kolhapur reservation – 1902 (i); Indra Sawhney – 16 Nov 1992 (iv).

s:
Assertion (A): NITI Aayog is a statutory body.
Reason (R): NITI Aayog was set up by a Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: A is false, R is true: NITI Aayog is an executive body created by a Cabinet resolution (1 Jan 2015), not by an Act of Parliament, so it is neither statutory nor constitutional.

s:
Assertion (A): The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities reports to the President, who lays the reports before each House of Parliament.
Reason (R): Article 350B was inserted by the 7th Amendment, 1956 on the recommendation of the States Reorganisation Commission.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both are true (Art. 350B duty to investigate and report to the President; inserted by the 7th Amendment on the SRC's recommendation), but the origin of the Article does not explain the reporting line, so R is not the explanation of A.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Women (NCW):
1. Its Chairperson, members and Member-Secretary are nominated by the President.
2. It is a statutory body under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990 and was constituted on 31 January 1992.
3. A commission for women had earlier been recommended by the Committee on the Status of Women in India (1974).
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: under Sec. 3 of the 1990 Act the Chairperson, five members and the Member-Secretary are all nominated by the Central Government, not the President.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Women:
1. Section 10 of the NCW Act, 1990 lists the functions of the Commission.
2. The Commission can impose criminal sentences on persons who violate the rights of women.
3. 'Mahila Jan Sunwai' is a public hearing of women's grievances organised by the Commission.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the NCW has the powers of a civil court while investigating and regulates its own procedure, but it cannot impose or enforce criminal sentences.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Person)
a. Jayanti Patnaik
b. Lalitha Kumaramangalam
c. Rekha Sharma
d. Vijaya Rahatkar
List-II (Tenure as NCW Chairperson)
i. From October 2024
ii. First Chairperson, 1992-95
iii. August 2018 – August 2024
iv. September 2014 – September 2017
x: Jayanti Patnaik – first chair 1992-95 (ii); Lalitha Kumaramangalam – Sep 2014 to Sep 2017 (iv); Rekha Sharma – chairperson Aug 2018 to Aug 2024 (iii); Vijaya Rahatkar – from Oct 2024 (i).

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC):
1. It was set up on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act and conforms to the Paris Principles.
2. Besides the Chairperson it has five full-time members, of whom two are persons with knowledge of human rights.
3. A member can be removed for proved misbehaviour by the President only after an inquiry by the Supreme Court.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: of the five full-time members (an SC judge, an HC Chief Justice and human-rights experts), three – not two – are human-rights experts, at least one a woman; there are also seven ex officio members.

s:
Consider the following statements about the NHRC:
1. The committee recommending its Chairperson includes the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and the Union Home Minister.
2. After the 2019 amendment, its Chairperson and members hold office for three years or up to the age of 70 years.
3. It cannot inquire into a matter after the expiry of one year from the date of the alleged violation.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: All three are correct. The 6-member committee is the PM (head), Lok Sabha Speaker, Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, Leaders of the Opposition in both Houses and the Home Minister (not the RS Chairman); the 2019 Act cut the term from 5 to 3 years (or 70); the one-year bar applies.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Chairperson of NHRC)
a. Justice Ranganath Misra
b. Justice H.L. Dattu
c. Justice Arun Kumar Mishra
d. Justice V. Ramasubramanian
List-II (Position)
i. 9th Chairperson, from December 2024
ii. 8th Chairperson, 2021-2024
iii. 1st Chairperson, 1993-96
iv. 7th Chairperson, 2016-2020
x: Ranganath Misra – first, 1993-96 (iii); H.L. Dattu – 7th, Feb 2016 – Dec 2020 (iv); Arun Kumar Mishra – 8th, Jun 2021 – Jun 2024 (ii); V. Ramasubramanian – 9th, from 30 Dec 2024 (i).

s:
Assertion (A): A State Human Rights Commission can inquire into violations of human rights relating to subjects in the Union List.
Reason (R): A State Human Rights Commission inquires only into matters in the State List and the Concurrent List that are not already before the NHRC or another statutory commission.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: A is false, R is true: under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 an SHRC inquires only into State List and Concurrent List matters, so Union List matters are outside it.

s:
Consider the following statements about State Human Rights Commissions:
1. The Andhra Pradesh State Human Rights Commission functions from Amaravati.
2. After 2019, a former Chief Justice or a judge of a High Court may be its Chairperson, and it has two other members.
3. The recommending committee is headed by the Chief Minister and includes the Speaker, the State Home Minister and the Leader of the Opposition.
Which of the above statements is/are NOT correct?
x: Only 1 is incorrect: the AP SHRC functions from Kurnool, not Amaravati. 2 and 3 are correct; the Governor appoints on the committee's recommendation but is not a member, and only the President can remove.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The NCPCR was set up in 2007 under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, with a Chairperson and six members.
2. The NCPCR monitors the implementation of the RTE Act 2009, the POCSO Act 2012 and the Juvenile Justice Act 2015.
3. India ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child on 11 December 1992, which treats a person below 16 years as a child.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong in part: India did accede on 11 Dec 1992, but the UNCRC defines a child as a person below 18 years, not 16.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Document)
a. Universal Declaration of Human Rights
b. CEDAW
c. Convention against Torture
d. UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
List-II (Year of adoption)
i. 1979
ii. 1989
iii. 1948
iv. 1984
x: UDHR – 1948 (iii); CEDAW – 1979 (i); Convention against Torture – 1984 (iv); UNCRC – 1989, in force 1990 (ii).

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Minorities (NCM):
1. A Minorities Commission was first set up by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs in 1978 and was made statutory by the NCM Act, 1992.
2. Jains were notified as a national minority in 2004.
3. Including the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson, the NCM has seven members.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 3). 2 is wrong: Jains were notified as the sixth minority on 27 January 2014, not 2004; the other five (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis) date from 1993. The Vice-Chairperson post was added in 1995.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis (NCSK):
1. It was constituted in 1994 under the NCSK Act, 1993 and became a non-statutory body after the Act lapsed in 2004.
2. It functions under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
3. Its tenure has most recently been extended up to 31 March 2028.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the NCSK works under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, not WCD. It investigates complaints and evaluates schemes but does not distribute relief.

s:
Assertion (A): The reports of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Women are laid before the State Legislature.
Reason (R): State commissions constituted under State laws report to the Governor or the State government.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: a commission created by a State law (here the AP Women's Commission Act, 1998) reports to the Governor/State government, which lays the report before the State Legislature.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Andhra Pradesh body)
a. AP State Human Rights Commission
b. AP Commission for Backward Classes
c. AP State Commission for Women
d. AP State Commission for SCs and STs
List-II (Feature)
i. Set up under a State Act of 2003
ii. Office at Mangalagiri
iii. Functions from Kurnool
iv. Permanent body under a 1993 State Act
x: AP SHRC – Kurnool (iii); AP BC Commission – permanent body under the 1993 Act (iv); AP Women's Commission – Mangalagiri (ii); AP SC/ST Commission – 2003 Act, reconstituted 2016 (i).

s:
Consider the following statements about State Lokayuktas:
1. Odisha was the first State to pass a Lokayukta law (1970), but its institution started functioning only in 1983.
2. Karnataka set up its Lokayukta, with its own Lokayukta Police wing, under an Act of 1986.
3. Uttarakhand was the first State to pass a Lokayukta Bill in 2011.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct (Odisha – first Act 1970, institution 1983; Uttarakhand – Bill of 1 Nov 2011). 2 is wrong: the Karnataka Lokayukta Act is of 1984; 1986 is Assam.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (State)
a. Bihar
b. Uttar Pradesh
c. Madhya Pradesh
d. Andhra Pradesh
List-II (Year of setting up the Lokayukta)
i. 1983
ii. 1975
iii. 1982
iv. 1973
x: Bihar – 1973 (iv); Uttar Pradesh – 1975 (ii); Madhya Pradesh – 1982 (iii); Andhra Pradesh – 1983 (i). Maharashtra (1971) was the first.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have both a Lokayukta and an Upa-Lokayukta.
2. By 2013, 21 States and one Union Territory had set up Lokayuktas.
3. Section 63 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 requires every State to establish a Lokayukta by its own law within one year of the Act's commencement.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Bihar, UP and Himachal Pradesh have a Lokayukta only; Rajasthan, Karnataka, AP and Maharashtra have both a Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Lokayukta in States:
1. It is appointed by the Governor, generally after consulting the Chief Justice of the High Court and the Leader of the Opposition.
2. It submits its annual consolidated report to the Chief Minister.
3. Its recommendations are advisory in most States but binding in some.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the annual consolidated report goes to the Governor, who lays it with an explanatory memorandum before the State Legislature – not to the CM, HC Chief Justice or Speaker.

s:
Assertion (A): Many State Lokayuktas are unable to investigate complaints independently.
Reason (R): Many Lokayuktas lack their own investigating wing and depend on the State police or Anti-Corruption Bureau.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: the notes list the lack of an own investigating wing (dependence on State police/ACB) and the absence of a uniform law as the key weakness of Lokayuktas.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Lokayukta looks into judicial and legislative acts as well as administrative actions of public servants.
2. The Chief Minister is excluded from the Lokayukta's jurisdiction in Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.
3. Justice N. Santosh Hegde's report on illegal iron-ore mining in Bellary (2011) led to the arrest of G. Janardhana Reddy.
Which of the above statements is/are NOT correct?
x: Only 1 is incorrect: the Lokayukta's jurisdiction is limited to administrative actions (corruption, maladministration), not judicial or legislative acts. 2 and 3 are correct; the CM is included in MP, Odisha, Gujarat and HP.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The first Lokpal Bill was introduced in the Fourth Lok Sabha in 1968 and passed by the Lok Sabha in 1969.
2. The first Lokpal Bill lapsed because the Rajya Sabha rejected it.
3. Under the original Lokpal Act a public servant had to declare assets within 30 days of entering office; after the 2016 amendment the form and manner are prescribed by the Central Government.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the 1968 Bill lapsed because the Lok Sabha was dissolved before the Rajya Sabha passed it, not because the Rajya Sabha rejected it.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Event relating to the Lokpal)
a. Rajya Sabha passed the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill with amendments
b. President's assent to the Act
c. Act came into force
d. Lokpal began functioning
List-II (Date)
i. 16 January 2014
ii. 27 March 2019
iii. 17 December 2013
iv. 1 January 2014
x: Rajya Sabha passage – 17 Dec 2013 (iii); assent – 1 Jan 2014 (iv); in force – 16 Jan 2014 (i); Lokpal began work – 27 Mar 2019 (ii).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Lokpal Bill, 2011:
1. It was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 4 August 2011 by P. Chidambaram.
2. It was examined by the Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice chaired by Abhishek Manu Singhvi.
3. The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill, 2011, the tenth attempt at such a law, became the 2013 Act.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the Bill was introduced on 4 Aug 2011 by V. Narayanasamy, Minister of State for Parliamentary Affairs, not P. Chidambaram.

s:
Assertion (A): The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 came into force on 1 January 2014.
Reason (R): The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 received the President's assent on 1 January 2014.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: A is false, R is true: 1 January 2014 is the date of assent; the Act came into force on 16 January 2014.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Ombudsman was first created in Sweden in 1809, and New Zealand (1962) was the first Commonwealth country to adopt it.
2. The term 'Lokpal' was coined by Dr. L.M. Singhvi in 1963.
3. Sweden's law of 1809 is also regarded as the world's first right-to-information law.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Sweden's first right-to-information law dates from 1766; 1809 is the Ombudsman.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Body)
a. Santhanam Committee (1962-64)
b. First Administrative Reforms Commission (1966)
c. Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2007)
d. Dr. L.M. Singhvi (1963)
List-II (Contribution)
i. Reiterated the recommendation for a Lokpal
ii. Coined the term 'Lokpal'
iii. Recommended the CVC and the CBI
iv. First recommended a Lokpal and State Lokayuktas
x: Santhanam Committee – CVC and CBI, not the Lokpal (iii); First ARC under Morarji Desai – Lokpal and Lokayuktas (iv); Second ARC – reiterated the Lokpal (i); L.M. Singhvi – coined 'Lokpal' (ii).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta:
1. It works under the AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1983, with the Upa-Lokayukta dealing with functionaries other than the higher ones.
2. The first Lokayukta of integrated Andhra Pradesh was Justice P. Lakshmana Reddy.
3. Its principal seat was shifted to Kurnool in 2021.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Only two (1 and 3). 2 is wrong: the first Lokayukta of integrated AP was Justice A. Sambasiva Rao; P. Lakshmana Reddy was the first after bifurcation.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta:
1. Ministers other than the Chief Minister and MLAs come within its purview.
2. It is appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of a selection committee for a five-year term.
3. In August 2026 Governor S. Abdul Nazeer appointed Justice (Retd) T. Mallikarjuna Rao as Lokayukta under Section 3(1) of the Act.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: All three are correct: the Act defines 'Minister' as a member of the Council of Ministers other than the CM, so the CM is outside but other Ministers and MLAs are within; appointment is by the Governor for 5 years; T. Mallikarjuna Rao was appointed in Aug 2026.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Body in Andhra Pradesh)
a. Lokayukta
b. State Vigilance Commission
c. Anti-Corruption Bureau
d. Upa-Lokayukta
List-II (Role)
i. Police agency for Prevention of Corruption Act offences
ii. Performs the Lokayukta's functions, as the Governor directs, when that office is vacant
iii. Statutory ombudsman under the 1983 Act reporting to the Governor
iv. Set up from 1964 on the pattern of the CVC
x: Lokayukta – statutory ombudsman, reports to the Governor (iii); State Vigilance Commission – from 1964 on the CVC pattern (iv); ACB – police agency for PC Act trap and DA cases (i); Upa-Lokayukta – acts when the Lokayukta's post is vacant (ii).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Lokpal:
1. Its Chairperson and members hold office for five years or till 70 years of age and are eligible for reappointment.
2. It consists of a Chairperson and not more than eight members, half of whom must be judicial members.
3. The minimum age for appointment is 45 years, and an eminent person needs 25 years' experience to be Chairperson.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the term is five years or age 70, but there is no reappointment; members also cannot be MPs or MLAs and are appointed by the President.

s:
Consider the following statements about the selection of the Lokpal:
1. The Selection Committee is chaired by the Prime Minister.
2. The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha are members of the Selection Committee.
3. The Search Committee consists of at least seven persons.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong in part: the LoP in the Lok Sabha is a member, but the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is not; the five are the PM, Lok Sabha Speaker, LoP in the Lok Sabha, CJI (or nominee judge) and an eminent jurist.

s:
Consider the following statements about the working of the Lokpal:
1. Its Inquiry Wing under Section 11 conducts preliminary inquiries into offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
2. It has superintendence over the CBI in all corruption cases investigated by the CBI.
3. A preliminary inquiry is ordinarily to be completed in 90 days and an investigation in six months, extendable by six months.
4. A trial by the Special Court is to be completed within one year, extendable up to two years.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Only three (1, 3 and 4). 2 is wrong: the Lokpal has superintendence over the CBI only in cases referred by the Lokpal, not in all CBI cases.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Person)
a. Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose
b. Justice A.M. Khanwilkar
c. Sushil Chandra
d. Prashant Mishra
List-II (Connection with the Lokpal)
i. Designed the Lokpal logo (2019)
ii. Non-judicial member, former Chief Election Commissioner
iii. Chairperson since 10 March 2024
iv. First Lokpal, appointed March 2019
x: P.C. Ghose – first Lokpal, appointed 19 Mar 2019 (iv); A.M. Khanwilkar – Chairperson since 10 Mar 2024 (iii); Sushil Chandra – non-judicial member, ex-CEC (ii); Prashant Mishra – logo designer (i).

s:
Assertion (A): Section 17A requires prior approval before an investigation into certain decisions of public servants.
Reason (R): Section 17A is a provision of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: A is true, R is false: Section 17A (prior approval before probe) belongs to the Prevention of Corruption Act, not the Lokpal Act; the SC gave a split verdict on it on 22 Jan 2026 (Nagarathna J – unconstitutional; Viswanathan J – contra).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC):
1. It was set up in February 1964 by an executive resolution and became statutory under the CVC Act, 2003, following the Vineet Narain case.
2. Its members hold office for five years or till the age of 65.
3. It consists of the Central Vigilance Commissioner and not more than two Vigilance Commissioners.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the term of the CVC and Vigilance Commissioners is four years or age 65, not five years.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Central Vigilance Commission:
1. The committee selecting the Central Vigilance Commissioner consists of the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
2. It has superintendence over the CBI in cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
3. A.S. Rajeev became the acting Central Vigilance Commissioner from 3 August 2026.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Only two (2 and 3). 1 is wrong: under Sec. 4 of the CVC Act the committee is the PM (chair), the Union Home Minister and the LoP in the Lok Sabha – not the CJI; the President appoints.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014:
1. It received the President's assent on 9 May 2014.
2. The Central Vigilance Commission is the competent authority for disclosures about central government employees.
3. Anonymous complaints can be taken up under the Act.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: anonymous complaints are not taken up; a public interest disclosure must identify the complainant, and there is a 7-year bar.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 2011 civil society movement for a Lokpal:
1. Anna Hazare of India Against Corruption fasted at Jantar Mantar in April 2011 and at Ramlila Maidan in August 2011.
2. The Joint Drafting Committee of April 2011 was chaired by Pranab Mukherjee with Prashant Bhushan as co-chairman.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: Pranab Mukherjee chaired the committee, but the co-chairman was Shanti Bhushan; Prashant Bhushan was a member.
